extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and patent/trademark practitioners registered to practice before the USPTO; counsel handling OED disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing registered practitioners' conduct before the USPTO (especially trademark practice), oversight of non-lawyers/third-party filers, disclosure/consent obligations, recordkeeping, and sanctions/procedures following violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.47 — aiding unauthorized practice by lack of oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.47 by aiding a non-lawyer/non-practitioner in the unauthorized practice of law through a lack of oversight or failure to monitor the activities of the non-lawyer/non-practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must adequately oversee and monitor non-lawyers/third-party entities to avoid facilitating the unauthorized practice of law before the Office; failure to monitor may constitute aiding unauthorized practice (e.g., non-lawyer listing herself as attorney, signing responses, or conducting interviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.49 — improper business relationship with non-practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.49 by engaging in a business relationship with a non-lawyer/non-practitioner where the activities of the business relationship consisted of the practice of trademark law before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must not maintain business arrangements with non-practitioners where the arrangement results in the non-practitioner performing or representing legal services before the USPTO on behalf of clients without proper authorization or supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) — accepting referred clients without consent after full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.62(a) by accepting referred clients from a referring entity without the consent of the referred client after full disclosure that the exercise of Respondent's independent professional judgment on behalf of the referred client would be or reasonably may be affected by the practitioner's own financial, business, property, or personal interests (e.g., Respondent's business relationship with the referring entity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a referral or business relationship creates a potential conflict that may affect independent professional judgment, the practitioner must make full disclosure to the client and obtain the client's informed consent before accepting representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) — third-party payment disclosure and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) by accepting compensation for legal services to or for a client from one other than the client without full disclosure to, and with consent of, the client, including not adequately describing the escrow and payment arrangement for trademark legal services performed for the referred clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must disclose and obtain client consent when legal fees will be paid by a third party and must adequately describe escrow/payment arrangements (e.g., whether fees are placed in a client trust account and how funds are segregated).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of trademark matters entrusted
rubrics_metrics.description: Violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) by neglecting trademark matters entrusted to him by not always adequately communicating with referred clients about their trademark registration applications and by not adequately supervising or monitoring the entity responsible for filing those applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must communicate adequately with clients about the status of matters, supervise third parties performing work on client matters, and take reasonable steps to assure that entrusted matters are properly handled and not neglected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to maintain custody/retain copies of client files and ensure confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not keep copies of trademark registration applications or other file materials he sent to the referring entity, and did not always take adequate measures to ensure and verify that TTG maintained the confidentiality of client matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should retain copies of client work product and client file materials they prepare and ensure that third parties maintain confidentiality; lack of custody or verification of confidentiality is a professional lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to verify filings, attorney of record, and correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not always take adequate measures to ensure and verify: (a) the trademark applications were, in fact, filed by TTG, (b) he was listed as the attorney of record on the trademark applications filed by TTG, and/or (c) that his address and telephone number were listed as the correspondence address on the trademark applications filed by TTG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After delegating filing to a third party, practitioners must verify that filings occurred correctly, that the attorney of record and correspondence information are accurate, and that they receive Office communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to monitor and receive Office communications and supervise third-party responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not always take adequate measures to: (a) ensure and verify that he received Office communications about the trademark applications he prepared and TTG filed and/or (b) monitor the activity of TTG with regard to the trademark applications he prepared and TTG filed, including steps that would have uncovered that Ms. Desmond had responded to Office communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must establish procedures to receive and act on Office communications and to monitor third-party activity (including ensuring third parties do not sign or file responses inappropriately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to inform clients about who will file and who is handling communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not always inform trademark applicants that he relied on TTG to file their applications and to maintain copies of their application files, nor did he always adequately communicate with clients about the status of their trademark registration applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must inform clients about who will file documents, who will handle communications, and otherwise keep clients reasonably informed about the status of their matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to act when alerted to potential unauthorized practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When informed that Ms. Desmond was representing herself as an attorney and/or engaging in the unauthorized practice of trademark law before the Office, Respondent did not take adequate steps to prevent Ms. Desmond from continuing to do so, such as regaining custody of client files from TTG and notifying the clients that Ms. Desmond was not an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon learning that a third party may be engaging in unauthorized practice, practitioners must take prompt remedial steps (e.g., regain files, notify clients, cease the relationship) to protect clients and comply with professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to investigate referring party's accounting and escrow practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent did not verify the exact amount of money collected by TTG for attorney fees, did not endeavor to learn whether TTG placed such fees in a client trust account to keep funds segregated, and did not discuss TTG's escrow accounting with TTG-referred applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should inquire into and verify how referring entities handle client funds (including whether fees are placed in trust accounts and whether fees are shared with non-lawyers) to ensure compliance with fiduciary and ethical obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating factors included: no prior disciplinary history during over fifty years registered as a patent practitioner; Respondent now fully understands his deviations from the standards and disciplinary rules; expressed sincere contrition; cooperated with the agency during investigation and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining discipline, the Office considers prior disciplinary history, demonstrated understanding and remediation, remorse, and cooperation as mitigating factors that may reduce sanction severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: public reprimand, probation, and suspension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreed sanction: public reprimand and placement on twenty-four months probation; if the OED Director believes Respondent during probation failed to comply, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, grant 15 days to respond, and request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to twenty-four months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discipline may include public reprimand and probation; noncompliance with probation or disciplinary rules can trigger an expedited show-cause/suspension process with set procedures and timelines (notice to respondent, 15 days to respond, forwarding record to USPTO Director).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and administrative actions upon suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall disseminate information per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; the USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; Respondent may not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension results in administrative steps to prevent practice (dissociation from customer numbers/PKI), public dissemination of discipline, and reinstatement requirements; procedural rules in 37 C.F.R. govern the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and client notification obligations after discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director will give notice of the public discipline to disciplinary agencies and courts and to the public. Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.20(a)(4), Respondent will, within thirty days, provide a copy of the Final Order to clients he is representing before the Office as of the date of the Final Order, and within forty-five days provide an affidavit to the OED Director stating he so notified those clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following discipline, the practitioner and the Office have explicit reporting/notification duties including public notice, notice to other disciplinary bodies, and the practitioner's obligation to notify current clients and attest to that notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the agreement prevents the Office from seeking further discipline for misconduct upon which an Order to Show Cause is issued, nor from considering the record of this proceeding (including the Final Order) in addressing further complaints or as an aggravating factor in future disciplinary proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior disciplinary record may be used as evidence or aggravating factor in future matters; settlement/resolution does not immunize from future discipline on the same or similar conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are published and made publicly available; practitioners should expect public reporting of disciplinary outcomes and notices to appear in official USPTO channels.
